items.title: Vedanta seeks premium over imported LNG prices for Rajasthan gas sale
items.rss_summary: Vedanta Oil and Gas Ltd is seeking a premium over imported LNG prices for 1.80 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) of natural gas from its Rajasthan block, putting the volume up for sale through an electronic auction. The three-month supply contract, running from January 1 to April 1, 2027, will be auctioned on December 14, according to a request for proposal dated November 20 and a draft gas sales agreement. Bidders have been asked to quote a premium they are willing to pay over the monthly average of Platts West India spot liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices, with the highest bids receiving priority in the allocation of available volumes. The starting premium is zero, with bids required to increase in increments of at least USD 0.05 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), according to the tender document. items.title: RBI approves SBI MF to acquire up to 9.99% stake in South Indian Bank
items.rss_summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has approved an SBI Mutual Fund's proposal to acquire up to a 9.99 per cent stake in private sector lender South Indian Bank, the bank said in a regulatory filing. The approval was communicated to the bank on November 23 and is subject to compliance with applicable regulatory conditions. "The RBI has accorded its approval to SBI Mutual Fund for acquiring aggregate holding of up to 9.99 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights in the Bank subject to the conditions specified therein," South Indian Bank said in the filing. The approval is subject to compliance with the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, RBI's Directions on Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights in Commercial Banks, 2025, the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, and other applicable laws and regulatory guidelines. items.title: Adani Group planning $120 bn in capex over next 5-6 years: Jefferies
items.rss_summary: Adani Group plans to invest more than USD 120 billion over the next five to six years across infrastructure, energy and data centres while seeking to keep net debt below 3.5 times earnings (EBITDA), according to a Jefferies research note on the group's annual conference. The group is leaning on its financial record as it expands in power, ports, transmission and data centres. At its annual investor conference, the group said its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio had declined from a peak of around 3.6-3.8 times during 2019-23. Group Chief Financial Officer Jugeshinder Singh highlighted lower borrowing costs, improving asset returns and a diversified funding base as evidence of stronger financial resilience, according to a Jefferies research note on the event. However, Jefferies' forecasts for six listed Adani companies put their aggregate net debt-to-EBITDA ratio at 3.7 times in FY27 and FY28, before declining to 3.4 times in FY29 and 3.1 times in FY30. items.title: Investors become richer by ₹34.61 trillion as Sensex surges in November
items.rss_summary: Equity markets have rallied sharply this month, with the BSE Sensex climbing nearly 11 per cent, making equity investors richer by Rs 34.61 lakh crore amid strong foreign fund inflows, lower crude oil prices, better-than-expected Q2 earnings and a global sell-off in AI-linked stocks. The 30-share BSE benchmark Sensex jumped 7,976.46 points, or 10.71 per cent till November 23. Following the bullish trend in equities, the market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies has surged by Rs 34.61 lakh crore to Rs 5,08,98,444.87 crore (USD 5.48 trillion) this month. Foreign investors have emerged as a major driver behind markets rally, with net investments crossing the Rs 1 lakh crore mark to reach Rs 1.27 lakh crore in November so far, marking the highest-ever monthly inflow. The strong inflows come after Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) withdrew Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data available with the NSDL. The stock closed at Rs 14.35 on Monday, compared with Rs 11.10 at the beginning of the month, reflecting growing market interest in the company's evolving business strategy and improving financial performance, according to stock exchange data. TAKE's consolidated profit after tax (PAT) stood at Rs 2.21 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 62 lakh in the corresponding period last year. Profit more than doubled from Rs 1.06 crore in the preceding quarter. Consolidated total income for the quarter was Rs 29.85 crore, including revenue from operations of Rs 29.41 crore.
